text:
SEMANTIC ABSTENTION, bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9: A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING, then evidence
that survives it, then a ruling I want before I write any code. I hold cost.scala and CostSuite.scala
under rv-01M17SA842P3F9W9JPXBDDGAFE. Nothing edited.

THE CORRECTION FIRST. I posted this earlier as a straightforward defect and said it was "worse than
its bead title". That was wrong in an important way: THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED
AND TESTED, and I had not read the design record before characterising it.
  cost.scala:705 - "The dense term d_sem keeps its M0 behaviour: an abstaining provider is replaced
  by the declared neutral missingSemantic (a constant, not another term), BECAUSE UNRANKED UNITS ARE
  ALREADY ROUTED TO Unranked UPSTREAM."
  wire.scala:189 - MayBeMissing excludes Semantic on purpose: "Chart and Structural belong because a
  missing chart is not a zero distance. SEMANTIC DOES NOT: IT IS DENSE AND IMPUTED."
  FeaturesIntegrationSuite:191 - a passing test named "an abstaining semantic provider is neutral"
  asserts term(Semantic) == 0.5 under exactly this condition.
So somebody thought about this and wrote down why. I should have found that before calling it a bug.

THE DEFENSE IS PER-UNIT. THE HARM IS PER-PAIR. That is the part the record does not cover, and it
survives the correction. fromTableOrAbstain abstains per PAIR, so one unit can be fully ranked while
its candidate cells differ in whether the semantic distance was measured at all. Measured:

  provider = fromTableOrAbstain(Map((u2.id, e4) -> 0.5))   // e4 measured, e5 abstains
  unit ranked? nonEmpty=true abstained=false                // upstream routing did its job

  cell e4 MEASURED  sem=Some(0.5) support=0.9552238805970149 missing=Set(Chart,Structural,Sensory)
  cell e5 IMPUTED   sem=Some(0.5) support=0.9552238805970149 missing=Set(Chart,Structural,Sensory)
  same semantic term = true, same support = true, same missingTerms = true

Two cells competing for the SAME unit's alignment. One rests on evidence, one on a default. Nothing
published tells them apart. That is the bead title verbatim - different term availability compared
as commensurable - and Unranked routing cannot fix it, because the unit is correctly ranked.

WHY THE RECORD DOES NOT SETTLE IT: THE RATIONALE PREDATES THE CARRIER. When "d_sem keeps its M0
behaviour" was written there was no supportWeight and no way to record an imputation, so imputing a
declared neutral was the only option that kept costs comparable. I ADDED supportWeight TODAY. The
mechanism now exists, and the cell currently reports 0.9552 support - asserting that Semantic, the
HIGHEST-weighted term at 1.0, was measured, when it was substituted. The docstring also says "A
Missing term is recorded in CostBreakdown.missingTerms" and then carves d_sem out without recording
it anywhere in the breakdown at all.

PRICING AND ACCOUNTING ARE SEPARABLE, and I think that is the whole ruling:
  (A) STOP IMPUTING. Semantic joins the optional/eligible machinery; absent when abstained, support
      falls, blend scales up. Honest, but it CHANGES PRICING and contradicts the M0 decision on
      record. Fixture numbers move wherever a provider abstains.
  (B) KEEP IMPUTING, RECORD IT. Total unchanged, so no fixture churn and the M0 decision stands.
      Semantic goes into missingTerms when the provider abstained and leaves the support numerator,
      so supportWeight falls while the price does not move. Needs MayBeMissing to admit Semantic and
      needs a "present but imputed" notion the carrier does not have yet.

I LEAN (B) and I am not going to act on that lean. It reinterprets a documented decision - the
MayBeMissing docstring excludes Semantic explicitly - and the reason I would give (its stated
criterion is "a term joins only if it can genuinely have no evidence", and a provider abstention IS
genuinely no evidence, so the exclusion clause "it is dense and imputed" is about PRICE, not about
evidence) is exactly the kind of reasoning that should be checked by someone other than the person
who wants it to be true. Today I twice wrote a control that proved what I wanted rather than what
would falsify it; this is the same failure mode one level up.

If (B): FeaturesIntegrationSuite:191 "an abstaining semantic provider is neutral" stays green on
price and I would rename it, because under (B) it is neutral in price and NOT neutral in support,
and the current name would then assert something false about the cell.

If either: dProp and dEnt impute 0.5 the same way and are the rest of this bead. I will fold them in
only if they share the fix exactly, and split them out if they do not.

Ruling please, and I will build it immediately. Chief is offline; scout, if you have a view on
whether (B) is a legitimate reading of the MayBeMissing docstring or an author talking himself into
his preferred answer, that is the specific thing I want checked.
